newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China to give listing priority to inland firms.
newsitem.headline: China to give listing priority to inland firms.

text.p: China is in the final stage of selecting a fourth batch of firms for overseas listings and plans to give priority to enterprises based in the centre and west of China, the official Securities Times said on Tuesday.

The paper said the China Securities Regulatory Commission, China's top securities watchdog, would mainly choose firms involved in basic industries with priority being given to companies headquartered in backward mid- and western China.

It quoted a commission official as saying Hong Kong would continue to be mainland China's chief overseas listing market, but China also aimed to list some enterprises in the United States or on other foreign stock markets.
Twenty-two mainland Chinese firms to date are listed on the Hong Kong bourse and two are listed in the U.S. with the listings having raised a total of US$4.4 billion, it said.
The official said overseas listing of Chinese companies had contributed substantially to China's ongoing economic reform and greatly improved the operations of the listed companies.
